name: sky_find
description: Search Starhop's catalogue for stars, constellations, planets, the Sun and Moon, deep-sky objects (Messier, Caldwell, NGC, IC) and named star patterns (asterisms). Use this whenever the learner's wording is ambiguous, misspelled, descriptive ('the seven sisters') or could match more than one thing, and before telling the learner that something does not exist. Returns up to 6 matches, each with a stable `ref` (for example con:Ori, star:27989, dso:M42, body:Mars, asterism:big-dipper) that the other tools accept, the kind of object, and whether it is above the horizon at the sky map's current time and place. It does not move the map.

query.description: Name or designation to look for, e.g. 'Orion', 'Betelgeuse', 'M42', 'andromeda galaxy', 'alpha Centauri', 'NGC 7000'.

name: sky_show
description: Open the sky map, select an object and glide the view so it is centred and framed, with its information panel open. This is the tool for 'show me', 'go to', 'find', 'where is', 'point at' and 'take me to' requests. `target` may be a ref from sky_find or a plain name; a plain name is resolved to the best catalogue match and the result says which object was chosen so you can tell the learner. The map makes sure the object is actually in view and the result's `presented` field says how: 'live' means it is up in the dark sky at the map's current time; 'time' means it was below the horizon or in daylight, so the map's clock was moved to its best time tonight (given in `clock_set_to`); 'atlas' means it is not visible tonight from the learner's location, so the map switched to the atlas, a chart of the whole sky with no horizon or time of day. Tell the learner in a few words when the clock moved or the atlas was used. Pass target 'none' to clear the current selection.

target.description: A ref such as con:Ori, star:Vega, dso:M31, body:Jupiter, asterism:big-dipper, or a plain name such as 'Orion'. 'none' clears the selection.

field_of_view_deg.description: Optional width of the view in degrees (1 to 150). Leave out to frame the object automatically.

name: sky_describe
description: Get Starhop's own facts about one object so you can answer questions accurately instead of from memory: what kind of object it is, brightness, distance, constellation, whether and when it is visible tonight from the learner's location, the months it is best seen, how to find it, what you will see, and for constellations the titles of the myths in the library. Use it before answering 'what is', 'how far', 'how bright', 'when can I see' and 'tell me about' questions. It does not move the map; call sky_show as well if the learner should see the object.

target.description: A ref from sky_find or a plain name. Use 'selected' for the object currently selected on the sky map.

name: sky_set_layers
description: Turn drawing layers of the sky map on or off. Only include the layers you want to change; everything else stays as it is. The change applies to the main sky map and is remembered. Use this for requests such as 'turn off lines', 'hide the labels', 'show the constellation pictures', 'show the grid', 'remove the ground' or 'just the stars' (turn everything except the horizon off).

constellation_lines.description: Stick-figure lines joining the stars of each constellation.

constellation_figures.description: Illustrated figures (the hunter, the bear) drawn behind the stars.

deep_sky_markers.description: Symbols for galaxies, clusters and nebulae.

deep_zoom.description: Load fainter stars and the full NGC/IC catalogue when zoomed in, like a telescope.

ecliptic.description: The ecliptic, the Sun's yearly path.

ground.description: Opaque ground below the horizon. Off lets the learner see the sky under their feet.

atmosphere.description: Daylight and twilight glow. Off shows the stars even in daytime.

milky_way.description: The band of the Milky Way.

name: sky_set_view
description: Move or zoom the sky map without selecting an object, or switch its mode. Use `face` to look toward a compass direction or straight up, `zoom` to step in or out, `field_of_view_deg` for an exact width, and `reset` to return to the default view facing north. `mode` switches between 'live' (the sky from the learner's location at the map's time, with a real horizon) and 'atlas' (a chart of the whole sky with no horizon and no time of day, where every object can be found). For looking at a named object use sky_show instead.

face.description: Direction to look. 'zenith' is straight up.

zoom.description: Zoom one step, or several steps for far_in / far_out.

field_of_view_deg.description: Exact width of the view in degrees, 1 (telescope) to 150 (whole sky).

reset.description: Return to the home view: facing north, wide field.

mode.description: live = real sky with horizon and clock; atlas = whole-sky chart with no horizon or time of day.

name: sky_set_time
description: Change the sky map's clock. Use `time` to jump to a moment, `shift_hours` or `shift_days` to move relative to the map's current time, and `speed` to pause or run the clock. Local times are in the learner's observing time zone, which is given in the context. Examples: 'tonight at 10' gives time '2026-11-11T22:00'; 'go back to now' gives time 'now'; 'six months from now' gives shift_days 182; 'speed up time' gives speed 'fast'. Jumping to a time pauses the clock unless you also set a speed.

time.description: 'now', or a local date and time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the learner's time zone.

shift_hours.description: Hours to move forward (positive) or back (negative) from the map's current time.

shift_days.description: Days to move forward or back from the map's current time.

speed.description: paused = frozen; real_time = 1 second per second; fast = 1 minute per second; faster = 1 hour per second; day_per_second shows the seasons; rewind = 1 hour per second backwards.

name: sky_set_location
description: Change where on Earth the learner is observing from. This changes which stars are visible, and it also changes Tonight and the course, so only use it when the learner asks to change or try a location ('show me the sky from Sydney', 'I am in Denver'). Give `city` to pick from Starhop's built-in list of about 90 cities, or give latitude, longitude and an IANA time zone for anywhere else. If the city is not in the list the result says so and suggests near matches.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone, e.g. 'America/Denver'. Required with latitude and longitude.

name.description: Label for a custom place, e.g. 'Denver, CO'.

name: sky_set_darkness
description: Set how dark the simulated sky is using the Bortle scale, which controls how many faint stars are drawn. 1 is a pristine dark site, 4 is rural, 6 is bright suburban, 8 to 9 is a city centre. Use for 'show me a dark sky', 'what would I see from the city' or 'show fewer stars'.

name: app_search
description: Search Starhop's learning content: course modules and lessons, star-hops (step-by-step routes between stars), asterisms, constellation pages and myths. Returns titles with a `path` you can pass to app_open. Use it for 'teach me about', 'is there a lesson on', 'how do I star-hop to' and 'what is the myth of' requests.

query.description: Topic or name, e.g. 'moon phases', 'Andromeda myth', 'Polaris', 'light pollution'.

name: app_open
description: Go to a page of the app. Use a `path` returned by app_search, or one of the section names: sky (the map), tonight (what is up tonight), month (this month's guide), calendar (visibility calendar), events (eclipses, meteor showers), learn (the course), library, constellations, myths, starhops, asterisms, stars, objects (deep-sky list), planets, practice (quizzes), review (items due), progress.

path.description: A section name from the list, or a path from app_search such as /learn/lesson/moon-phases.
